best_for: PC gamers who want to stream games from their own Windows or Linux machine to a laptop, TV or phone running Moonlight, without a cloud service.

points.title: You need Moonlight on the other end
points.text: Sunshine is the host side only. You play on another device through a Moonlight client, which runs on many phones, TVs and computers.

points.title: Uses your graphics card's encoder
points.text: It encodes video on NVIDIA (NVENC), AMD (AMF) or Intel (QuickSync) hardware, and on Linux through VAAPI. A software encoder is the fallback when no supported GPU is present.

points.title: Hardware and network floor
points.text: The listed minimum is an AMD Ryzen 3 or Intel Core i3, 4 GB of RAM, and 5 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11ac) on both host and client. On Windows, Intel graphics must be Skylake or newer. The project marks this list as a work in progress.

points.title: Windows 11 is the stated floor
points.text: The supported list names Windows 11 or later, Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 13+, Fedora 43+, FreeBSD 15.1+ and macOS 15+. The Windows installers here are x64 and ARM64 and install for all users.

points.title: Set up from a browser
points.text: Settings and pairing with clients happen in a web page, either on the host or from your phone.

points.title: Free, and the Flatpak is official
points.text: Sunshine is open source under GPL-3.0. Flathub marks its Flatpak as verified, published by LizardByte, for x64 and ARM64. The Windows listing keeps 24 versions; Linux lists only the current release.
